feedback: If a learner applies 'rotate' to the yearly orbit or 'revolve' to the daily spin, separate them with the body or the model: rotate = spin on the spot (day/night); revolve = walk a lap around (the year). Have them rehearse each in a sentence with its effect.

If a learner reverses waxing/waning or thinks the Moon physically grows, restate: waxing = lit part growing towards full; waning = lit part shrinking towards new; the Moon itself is not changing size.

If a learner attaches a term to the wrong event (e.g. 'the equinox is the longest day') or coins a hybrid like 'revolvation', do NOT drill definitions or penalise — keep offering contexts that use the words correctly so the right form and meaning settle through use.
Reinforce correct use: 'Yes — Earth's rotation makes day and night, and its revolution round the Sun makes the year. You used each word for the right motion.'
activities.intendedInsight: Rotation (spin on the axis, once a day → day and night) and revolution/orbit (travel around the Sun, once a year → the year, and with the tilt the seasons) are two different motions of the same Earth; waxing/waning describe the lit part of the Moon growing/shrinking; solstice/equinox mark day-length events. Each term is bound to a motion or event the child can see and describe.
learnerActions: Apply a word to a model of the Earth–Moon–Sun system and watch it perform the motion that word names: choose 'rotation' and see the Earth spin on its axis; choose 'revolution' and see the Earth travel around the Sun.

Apply BOTH 'rotation' and 'revolution' to the SAME Earth, one after the other, and describe out loud the two different motions that play — the spin that makes a day versus the orbit that makes a year.

Apply 'waxing' to a Moon and describe the lit part growing towards full; apply 'waning' and describe the lit part shrinking towards new. Say aloud that the Moon itself is not changing size — only the lit portion we see.
Place 'solstice' and 'equinox' at the correct points on a tilted Earth's year-path and say what each marks (longest or shortest day for a solstice; roughly equal day and night for an equinox).

After each action, say a full sentence that uses the word with the effect it causes, e.g. 'Earth's rotation on its axis causes day and night' and 'Earth's revolution around the Sun, with its tilt, causes the seasons.'
activities.title: Name-the-motion model: bind each word to what it does
